title: Layered configuration load with a defined precedence order
contract: Six ordered layers resolved at every startup: inherited shell -> ~/.hermes/.env (override=True) -> ~/.hermes/.op.env (override=False, only if the bootstrap token is unset) -> project .env (override only when no user file existed) -> external vaults -> managed /etc/hermes/.env (override=True, deliberately last), then _reapply_terminal_config_bridge() re-asserts config.yaml-owned terminal.* keys over whatever .env supplied. hermes_cli/env_loader.py:468-560; entry env-vars.precedence. Long-lived processes re-run the whole load per turn, which is why the bridge is re-applied (issues #29186, #67323). HERMES_HOME / HERMES_PROFILE / XDG_* select which files those are.
governance: read-only at load time; a reload that re-reads credentials must not widen posture flags mid-process, so posture flags stay pinned at boot and only non-posture keys hot-reload
remaining_verbatim:
- A managed/operator overlay layer applied last (e.g. a system-wide .env) that the owner's files cannot override
- An external-vault layer in the env load order
- Reload without restart (re-read the layers, report changed and removed keys)
- Re-assert settings-owned keys over .env after a reload

title: Admin-pinned managed scope an owner-level edit cannot override
contract: $HERMES_MANAGED_DIR/.env, default /etc/hermes/.env, root-owned, applied LAST with override=True so it beats the user's file and any shell export. managed_scope.is_env_managed(key) is a predicate every writer consults, and save_env_value() refuses with 'Cannot set {key}: it is managed by your administrator ({src}) and cannot be changed.' (hermes_cli/config.py:4556). The inventory is honest that v1 enforcement is filesystem permissions only — an agent can still mutate os.environ in-process (design section 8.1). Entry env-vars.dotenv-managed, plus HERMES_MANAGED (coarse write lock) and HERMES_MANAGED_DIR.
governance: read-only itself, but it must be the floor the kernel reads: a pinned posture key has to be unwritable by the config.write action kind, and the refusal must be an audited event

title: Writer allowlist for names that hijack execution or soften posture
contract: _ENV_VAR_NAME_DENYLIST (hermes_cli/config.py:207, enforced at :271) blocks the generic writer — dashboard, MCP install flow, API — from persisting LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/PYTHONSTARTUP, NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH, PATH, SHELL, BROWSER, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, HERMES_HOME/PROFILE/CONFIG, HERMES_OPTIONAL_MCPS, the ACP subprocess selectors, and the policy flags HERMES_YOLO_MODE / HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS / HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS / HERMES_EXEC_ASK. Enforced on write only; the MCP install route adds a second gate that only catalog-declared names may be written (hermes_cli/web_routers/mcp.py:508). Entry env-vars.write-denylist.
governance: PRIVILEGED — this is the parameter validation of the config.write kind. A name outside the registry is refused before authorization, the same shape as capability_actions.py:139 refusing a missing required param before the kernel is consulted
remaining_verbatim:
Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. #1179 changed nothing on this row's subject: its client.py change is an outbound disclosure (cwd_secret_files :225-249 and the "withholding is undercut" WARNING in _merged_env :554-600), not a name policy or a writer. Neither did the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1: tool_patterns_over_bounds, a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ and a tools_allow/tools_deny bounds refusal in admin_mcp_add) — it touches no env name, writer or override path and only moved line numbers. H502 (#1174) did change item 3 and half of item 2, and that is folded in here. Three items owed, two shippable today against real surfaces:

1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No general env-name registry exists and no `config.write` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py. The one writer that persists env-var names to pass into a process today (H255's ${env:NAME} setting references are only read), H595's llm.execute_code_env_passthrough setting and skill declarations, is gated by code_env._passable_name (agents/core/code_env.py:89-101, enforced at agents/core/settings_db.py:1183-1189), a denylist (since RB-2 it also refuses the NERVA_<X> spelling of a hub variable and a NERVA_* credential) that still passes NODE_PATH, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, BROWSER and GIT_SSH_COMMAND; owed there: refuse those names too, or replace the denylist with the declared-names registry. Of Hermes' hijack names, PATH, SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:167), NODE_PATH (:176) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are named as members of the two OUTBOUND allowlists, and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 (pinned dropped at tests/test_nerva_import.py:825). Design consequence: the outbound lists cannot double as the write-side registry — they deliberately admit the plumbing names Hermes forbids on write — so the registry is a separate, inbound-only list. When any env/config writer lands, that allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:147-151 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :159-160.

2. THE MCP `env` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED (shippable now; the "untested" half closed with #1174). MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:145-156) sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes `POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it — reproduced end to end at HEAD through TestClient (200 {"ok": true}; stored MCPServer.env == {}; to_config() has no env key). The field it would populate is live — MCPServer.env (agents/core/mcp/client.py:443) → _merged_env (:554-600) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:476-483). Already pinned by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522: `env` is not a MCPServerConfig field, to_config (:913-927) does not export it and load_from_config (:929-970) does not read it. Reachability: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449) and no CLI adds servers, so the raw admin API is the only path today. Still owed: `extra="forbid"` (or an explicit named refusal) on MCPServerConfig, plus a test asserting the route refuses an `env` body rather than swallowing it — and the same refusal must cover the hijack names above on the day `env` becomes operator-settable.

3. PER-SERVER `env` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:286-287; docstring :260 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does `merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env)` with no filter (:598-599). The "decide whether the baseline should become the default" half of this item is DONE: since H502 the baseline is on unless JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 (:184-195; docs/FLAGS.md "on by default since H502") and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins both directions, so the legacy branch is now the explicit escape hatch rather than the shipped path. Owed: gate per-server overrides on the item-1 write-side registry (NOT merely on STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST + _SECRET_LIKE — that policy passes PATH, SHELL, NODE_PATH and would pass an operator-supplied PATH/NODE_PATH override untouched), or make the bypass an explicitly reviewed, audited exception. Severity, checked directly rather than inferred: LATENT. `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field, the admin route constructs MCPServer without one (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:226-238), and the dedicated WorldView override caller has been retired; the generic in-process override API remains. No untrusted input reaches the override loop, so this is a boundary to close before `env` becomes operator-settable, not a live hole. The outbound allowlist's one intentional exception — a name the owner lists in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:263-267, :279-282; tests :449-503) — is owner-declared and host-wide, and is not this row's write boundary.

title: Secrets resolved from an external vault instead of a plaintext file
contract: agent/secret_sources/registry.py:425 apply_all() pulls from enabled vaults into os.environ after dotenv, with documented precedence (preserve_existing > pre-existing env > mapped sources > bulk sources, first claim wins, per-source wall-clock timeout, conflict warnings), profile aliasing of FOO_<PROFILE> onto canonical FOO, and a provenance map _SECRET_SOURCES that setup and hermes model read to label where a credential came from. Built-ins: Bitwarden Secrets Manager via the bws CLI, 1Password via op:// refs, a generic command source; plugins register more via PluginContext.register_secret_source(). Entries env-vars.secret-sources-registry, -bitwarden, -onepassword, env-vars.dotenv-op.
governance: read-only (resolution). The credential must keep landing in the broker/store and never in os.environ, so redaction and the inject-at-approval property hold

- The older VaultResolver (agents/core/secrets_vault.py) remains a separate single-backend path used only by oauth.py

title: Response pacing that imitates a human typing
contract: HERMES_HUMAN_DELAY_MODE (off / natural / custom), HERMES_HUMAN_DELAY_MIN_MS, HERMES_HUMAN_DELAY_MAX_MS — deliberate latency so the bot's replies do not read as machine-fast. Adjacent in intent: BROWSERBASE_ADVANCED_STEALTH, CAMOFOX_* stealth browser.
governance: read-only; the reason to refuse is product principle, not privilege
historical_exclusion_reason: Skip on product grounds and keep it skipped. Nerva's stated posture is honesty — an honesty badge in the HUD, provenance on recall, refusals that name their reason. A knob whose only purpose is to make a machine pass as a person contradicts that at the level of principle, and it would sit oddly beside an approval queue built on the owner knowing exactly what acted and when. No re-open path.
